our_title: Fallback path of coarse-separator uncoarsening returns without freeing its exchange buffer group
ran:
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=buildp/lib ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 mpirun --oversubscribe -np 3 ./dtest_buildp 4elt.grf -1 order "$(cat st_z.txt)" 0 n -  (st_z: low=z so that every coarse separator has an empty part)
pristine: 6 LeakSanitizer records over the 3 ranks: '#2 ... in vdgraphSeparateMlUncoarsen .../vdgraph_separate_ml.c:399' (memAllocGroup) below '#3 ... vdgraphSeparateMl2 vdgraph_separate_ml.c:775'; all ranks OrderCompute rc=0.
patched (build): same command, 0 records mentioning vdgraph_separate_ml.c, rc=0 on all ranks.
severity_note: Same as the review: a leak of about 5 Gnum per process-count plus 2-3 Gnum per coarse vertex, on a normal fallback path repeated at every nested-dissection level where it occurs; no crash.
evidence: vdgraph_separate_ml.c:449-454: 'if (reduglbtab[0] == 1) { /* If all possible partitions are invalid */ #ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_BDGRAPH2 errorPrintW (...); #endif return (1); }' while the memory-error branch just above (:443-447) does 'if (vsndcnttab != NULL) memFree (vsndcnttab);'. Same routine uses SCOTCH_DEBUG_BDGRAPH1/2 (:383, :388, :390, :450, :452) instead of the VDGRAPH flags.
review_accuracy: Mechanism, location and reproducer accurate. Its second fix option ('allocate after the check, as bdgraphBipartMlUncoarsen does') would copy the twin's weaker structure: there the post-check allocation is only agreed upon under SCOTCH_DEBUG_BDGRAPH1, so a release-mode allocation failure returns on one process only (hang); the vdgraph ordering, which piggybacks the allocation flag on the best-separator reduction, is the better of the two and should be kept.
first_pass_critique: Status, reproducer and preferred option right. Its DMO-05 patch sketch silently mixes in an unrelated hunk (ABS on reduloctab[4], which is DMO-11), and it did not notice that the debug code of this routine is compiled under the Bdgraph debug flags (fixed in the same commit here). Its option B tradeoff text is right that the twin's second agreement is debug-only.

extra_instances.quote: allocation after the validity check, agreed only '#ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_BDGRAPH1'

fix_options.label: A: free the group leader on the all-invalid path (and use the Vdgraph debug flags)
fix_options.summary: memFree (vsndcnttab) before the fallback return; vsndcnttab is non-NULL there since reduglbtab[5] == 0 means every allocation succeeded.
fix_options.tested: LSan run above (0 records after), check_scotch_dgraph_order / check_prog_dgord / ptcheck 32- and 64-bit, DEBUG_ALL tree run
fix_options.tradeoffs: No behaviour change; keeps the release-mode agreement on allocation failures.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Precedent: the memory-error branch three lines above frees the same leader; the maintainer's 7.0.17 fixes of this kind are one-line frees (e.g. 'free column block tree of compressed ordering on...' in the combined series, and his own 'free data buffer of forked de-compression task').

fix_options.label: B: allocate after the validity check, bdgraph structure
fix_options.summary: Move the memAllocGroup below the all-invalid return and add a second (debug-only collective) agreement on it.
fix_options.tested: untested: applies cleanly (git apply --check); not built
fix_options.tradeoffs: Saves a transient allocation on the fallback path but makes a release-mode allocation failure non-collective (a failing process returns alone), i.e. trades a leak for a hang; this is the twin's DMO-03-class weakness.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would not take a change that weakens error agreement; G22 should rather align bdgraph on the vdgraph structure.

cleanup_done: none needed (the debug-flag fix removes a copy-paste leftover of the twin)
notes: The leak fires for every ML level whose coarse separators are all invalid; with the default strategies this is rare, with low=z it is systematic. Tooling (all under repro/common/): dtest.c = driver linked with libptscotcherr (non-exiting errorPrint) and MPI_Init_thread(MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE) (the first pass's drv.c and my first driver used MPI_Init: fold-dup coarsening then hangs at random, which invalidated several 'hang' readings until fixed); fishim.c = G18's LD_PRELOAD injector plus an FI_FUNC filter (only allocations whose backtrace contains the routine are counted), scan.sh = G18's scanner; trees: build (series, 32-bit ASan+UBSan), buildp (base-combined, same flags), build64 (series, 64-bit), buildfi/buildfip (base/series, UBSan only, for LD_PRELOAD), builddbg (series, -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL). Base of every 'pristine' run is base-combined (v7.0.17 + the 142-commit combined series), which is identical to v7.0.17 for every file of this group.

our_title: Separator store omits local part loads; restored separators carry stale anchor loads into band graphs
ran:
Proof on the -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree (repro/common/dmo12proof.sh, output dmo12proof.txt): strategy n{sep=(q{strat=h}|z)b{width=3,strat=q{strat=f}},ole=s,ose=s,osq=s}, np=3, 4elt.grf.
B (base-combined vdgraph.h + vdgraph_store.c swapped into the series tree, i.e. pristine store + the new vdgraphCheck test): '(0): ERROR: vdgraphCheck: invalid local part loads' and '(0): ERROR: vdgraphStoreUpdt: inconsistent graph data' on all 3 ranks (vdgraphStoreUpdt calls vdgraphCheck under SCOTCH_DEBUG_VDGRAPH2).
A/C (full series): no error, rc=0 on all ranks. Also run on the DEBUG tree with the default strategy: clean.
read_only: The quality effect of the stale anchor loads on dgraphBand was not measured (as in the first pass).
severity_note: As the review: wrong (possibly negative) anchor loads only affect the balance of the band separation after a '|' selection; no crash.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/vdgraph.h:74-82 (VdgraphStore); vdgraph_store.c:117-123 (save), :146-155 (restore); vdgraph_check.c:230-236 (local sizes only); consumer vdgraph_separate_bd.c:109-110
evidence: vdgraph.h:74-82: VdgraphStore has fronglbnbr, compglbloaddlt, compglbload[2], compglbsize0, complocsize0, fronlocnbr, datatab and no complocload; vdgraph_store.c:146-155 restores compglbload/compglbsize/complocsize only; vdgraph_check.c:238-258 reduces the recomputed complocload[] into global sums and compares them with compglbload[] but never with grafptr->complocload[].
review_accuracy: Accurate, including the vdgraphCheck remark; its fix line is what was done.
first_pass_critique: Status and instrumented reproduction right; its option A is the fix taken. It saved complocload[3] whereas the store convention derives the third value (as compglbload[2] and complocsize[1] are), and it left the 'vgraphCheck:' routine-name typos in the two messages next to the new test. Its 'related latent bug' (PS-DMO-1) is the same defect seen from the consumer side, see PS-DMO-1.

our_title: Zero method's global-size shortcut is correct once the store restores every local field
ran: Same runs as DMO-12 (dmo12proof.txt): with the store fixed, the strategy (q{strat=h}|z)b{...} passes vdgraphCheck after every vdgraphStoreUpdt and after the z method on the DEBUG_ALL tree, with the shortcut in vdgraphSeparateZr unchanged.
severity_note: The observed symptom (stale complocload reaching vdgraphSeparateBd) is real but is DMO-12's defect; the shortcut itself is sound.
evidence: vdgraph_separate_zr.c:78: 'if (grafptr->compglbsize[0] != grafptr->s.vertglbnbr) vdgraphZero (grafptr);' is the exact twin of vgraph_separate_zr.c: 'if (grafptr->compsize[0] != grafptr->s.vertnbr) vgraphZero (grafptr);'. compglbsize[0] == vertglbnbr implies all vertices are in part 0 on every process, hence complocload[0] == velolocsum etc., provided the graph is consistent, which the store now guarantees (and vdgraphCheck enforces under SCOTCH_DEBUG_VDGRAPH2).
first_pass_critique: The finding is a restatement of DMO-12 from the consumer side. Its preferred option (always call vdgraphZero) would add a memset of the whole part array to every 'z' call to work around a store omission, and would diverge from the sequential twin; the first pass itself listed 'fix the store' as option B.

fix_options.label: A: fix the store (DMO-12) and keep the shortcut
fix_options.summary: No change to vdgraphSeparateZr.
fix_options.tradeoffs: none
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors vgraphSeparateZr; the store is the single place that must restore a consistent graph.

fix_options.label: B: always call vdgraphZero
fix_options.summary: Drop the test in vdgraphSeparateZr.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Hides inconsistencies instead of fixing them; extra memset per call; diverges from the sequential twin.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He keeps the twins identical.

notes: Resolved by the DMO-12 commit; listed as not-a-bug because the code it points at is correct.

our_title: Diffusion separator hides allocation failure in a summed degree and falls through after freeing
ran:
Fault injection on the UBSan-only trees (LD_PRELOAD fishim.so, FI_FUNC=vdgraphSeparateDf, FI_RANK=1, np=3, strategy st_df.txt which puts d{pass=3} inside the band graphs of the ordering ML):
pristine (repro/common/scan_df_pristine.txt): 'nth=3 exit=139 :: (1): ERROR: vdgraphSeparateDf: out of memory; vdgraph_separate_df.c:177:28: runtime error: store to null pointer of type float; signal 11' and the same at nth=11 (second Df call). The -1 of rank 1 was swallowed by the positive degrees of ranks 0 and 2.
patched (scan_df_patched.txt): 'nth=3 exit=0 :: (1): ERROR: vdgraphSeparateDf: out of memory; (0),(1): ERROR: vdgraphSeparateBd: cannot separate band graph; rank 0/1/2: OrderCompute rc=0' (the band separation fails on all processes of that sub-communicator and the ML low strategy takes over). nth=11 idem.
read_only: The 'detected then fall-through' branch (sum < 0) could not be hit with 3 processes, as the first pass said; read: :141-144 has no return and :145-149 then dereferences/free()s the NULL leader.
severity_note: As the review: needs an allocation failure, but then a NULL store on the failing process (crash) in a method used by default strategies.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/vdgraph_separate_df.c:123-149 (flag :128, reduction :136, branch without return :141-144, use :147 and :177)
evidence: vdgraph_separate_df.c:127-128: 'errorPrint ("vdgraphSeparateDf: out of memory"); reduloctab[0] = -1;' then :136 'MPI_Allreduce (reduloctab, reduglbtab, 4, GNUM_MPI, MPI_SUM, ...)'; :141-144 'if (reduglbtab[0] < 0) { if (ielsloctax != NULL) memFree (ielsloctax + grafptr->s.baseval); }' (no return).
review_accuracy: Accurate for both files. Its 'reduce a separate error flag with MPI_MAX' would add a second collective where a summed slot in the existing reduction does the same.
first_pass_critique: Right status and evidence; its option A is the design taken (5th summed slot, test first, return). Its sketch put 'reduloctab[4] = 0' before the allocation and kept it unconditional, which is fine; the committed version sets it in the else branch so that the slot is written exactly once per path. Its claim that the injected run showed 'OrderCompute/Map returns on all ranks' could not have been observed with its driver (MPI_Init without MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE makes fold-dup coarsening hang at random), so its hang readings are unreliable.

our_title: dmapSave never rejects inconsistent vertex counts and dereferences fragments without part array
ran:
Internal-API driver repro/common/dmaptest.c (dgraphLoad, dmapInit, one hand-made fragment per process, dmapSave), np=3, 4elt.grf:
pristine (dmaptest_buildp): mode x (root fragment claims vertlocnbr+1 vertices): rc=0 on all ranks, file header 15607 for a 15606-vertex graph, 15607 data lines; mode n (root fragment without part array): 'dmapping_io.c:196:19: runtime error: load of null pointer of type Anum' + ASan SEGV.
patched (dmaptest_build): mode x: '(0),(1),(2): ERROR: dmapSave: invalid mapping (1)', rc=1 on all ranks, nothing written; mode n: 'dmapSave: invalid mapping (2)' on all ranks, rc=1, no hang; mode c (complete): rc=0, 15606 lines, identical to pristine.
Forwarded lead (NULL part array from a user strategy): pristine 'mpirun -np 3 build/bin/dgpart 4 4elt.grf /dev/null -m"r{sep=q{strat=f}}"' -> 'dmapping_io.c:256:34: runtime error: load of null pointer' + SEGV; and './dtest_buildp 4elt.grf -1 map "r{sep=q{strat=f}}" 4 n -' -> 'dmapping.c:224:47: runtime error: load of null pointer' + SEGV in dmapTerm (SCOTCH_dgraphMap). Patched: dgpart writes a valid 15607-line mapping file (parts 0,1,2 at np=3) and SCOTCH_dgraphMap returns 0 on all ranks (fixed at the source by patch 0010).
G20's guard (alt/PS2-G05-dmapSave-null-parttab-guard.diff), applied to the pristine UBSan tree and run with the non-exiting error library and no user part array (so that only dmapSave sees the fragments): np=1 'dmapSave: invalid mapping (4)' rc=1; np=3: rank 2 prints the error and breaks out of its send loop, the root never returns: HANG (30 s timeout), see repro/common/redo.txt.
severity_note: The dead test itself is low (needs a corrupted mapping); the forwarded NULL-part-array crash is medium (reachable from any user 'r{...}' strategy without seq=, through SCOTCH_dgraphMap/dgpart -m), fixed at its source in patch 0010 and rejected in dmapSave in patch 0008.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/dmapping_io.c:123-126 (dead test); :196 and :256 (part array dereferences); kdgraph_map_rb_part.c:133 (fragment with NULL part array)
evidence: dmapping_io.c:123: 'if ((reduglbtab[1] < 0) && (reduglbtab[1] > grafptr->procglbnbr))' (reduloctab[1] = dmapptr->vertlocnbr, summed); the sibling dmapTerm (dmapping.c:202-211) accepts exactly 'reduglbtab[0] == 0' or '== grafptr->vertglbnbr'. kdgraph_map_rb_part.c:133: 'fragptr->parttab = kgrfdat.m.parttax + kgrfdat.s.baseval;' with parttax NULL when kgraphMapSt ran a strategy that computes no mapping (stratdummy default of 'seq').
review_accuracy: Accurate on the dead test. Its fix ('|| and vertglbnbr') would accept partial mappings, which the sibling dmapTerm rejects; the committed test is the dmapTerm one (empty or complete).
first_pass_critique: Right status; it preferred the range form and flagged the exact-match form as 'could reject a legitimate partial mapping' without checking dmapTerm, which already requires completeness. The forwarded PS2-G05-1 lead was located correctly by G05 but G20's guard (per-loop 'break') is wrong: on a non-root process it skips the sends the root is waiting for (hang shown above). Neither noticed that dmapTerm dereferences the same NULL array first for API users.

our_title: Label gathers of ordering writers use based displacements into un-based arrays: overflow, shifted output
ran:
lbl.grf = 12-vertex path, baseval 1, labels 101..112 (repro/common/).
pristine ASan tree: 'mpirun --oversubscribe -np 3 buildp/bin/dgord lbl.grf ord.out' -> ord.out: '12 / -1094795586 106 / 101 107 / 102 108 / ... / 109 -1094795586 / 110 101 / 111 102' (first column = label of the previous vertex, first entry uninitialized; same at np=1 and 2). dgord -T (dorderSaveTree2) prints correct labels by accident (reads are shifted like the writes).
Heap overflow proof with glibc malloc (UBSan-only tree, lbl14.grf = 14 vertices so that the 168-byte group is chunk-aligned): 'mpirun -np 1 buildfi/bin/dgord lbl14.grf o.out' -> 'Fatal glibc error: malloc.c:2601 (sysmalloc): assertion failed ... Aborted'; np=3 -> 'munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer, Aborted'; 'dgord lbl14.grf /dev/null -Tt.out' (dorderSaveTree2's 56-byte array) -> same aborts at np=1 and 3.
patched: ord.out '12 / 101 107 / 102 108 / ... / 112 103' (np=3; identity at np=1), -T output unchanged, lbl14 runs exit 0 at np=1 and 3; new check line 'dgord data/m4x4_b1_elv.grf ... -T...' passes at np=1,2,3,4 (pristine prints '-1094795586' labels on it).
severity_note: Higher than the review's medium: a heap write past a malloc'ed block (glibc aborts shown) plus a silently wrong ordering file from the shipped dgord tool for every based, labeled graph.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/dorder_io.c:120-123 (un-based allocation), :144-145 (gather with based procdsptab), :203 (late basing); dorder_io_tree.c:118 (allocation), :130-131 (gather), :151 (based use by orderSaveTree/orderSaveMap, whose parameter is named vlbltax)
evidence: dorder_io.c:144-145: 'commGatherv (grafptr->vlblloctax + grafptr->baseval, grafptr->vertlocnbr, GNUM_MPI, vlbltax, grafptr->proccnttab, grafptr->procdsptab, ...)' with vlbltax straight from memAllocGroup (:123) and ':203 vlbltax -= ordeptr->baseval;' only afterwards. dmapping_io.c:170 (fixed by 4290e22): 'vlbltax -= grafptr->baseval; /* Base label array since displacement array is based */' before the same commGatherv.
review_accuracy: Accurate; 'prints the previous vertex's label on every line' confirmed for both columns. For dorder_io_tree.c the output is right but the overflow is real (glibc abort above), which the review did not distinguish.
first_pass_critique: Right reproduction of dorderSave; it could not show the overflow (ASan does not see MPI's copies) and stopped there, while glibc's own checks on a chunk-aligned size prove it. Its diff left dorder_io.c's vlbltax uninitialized on non-root processes and kept the name vlbltab for an array it based.
